Diamond prices turned up in August, with the Rapaport Trade Diamond Index's one-carat category gaining 0.5% — its first rise in fifteen months.

The smaller sizes did better still: the 0.50-carat added 2.5% and the 0.30-carat 2.0%, while the three-carat broke an eighteen-month run of stability and fell 0.4%. Rapaport credits the recovery to supply discipline, not returning demand — miners and manufacturers cut production, and the categories that fell hardest in 2025 rebounded as the imbalance closed.

Gold rose 2.77% to $4,426.80 Thursday morning against Wednesday's mark on this paper's tape, its first higher reading since 28 August after four straight lower marks.

Palladium moved hardest, up 4.82% to $1,348.00, ahead of silver's 3.18% gain to $65.58 and platinum's 2.86% climb to $1,762.00. The recovery reclaims 40.17% of the $297.00 gold lost since 28 August; the ounce is still $177.70 below that mark.
